header: THE CONTRACT OF A TOPIC. Every subject the search bar knows about (a calculator, a converter, the tyre reader, the VIN reader, the BH-series guide, a live-data card) is ONE folder in src/tools/<topic>/: <topic>.ts the pure logic (a calculation, a reading, a table), with its own selftest <Something>.tsx its cards and forms (React) topic.ts WHAT THE SEARCH LINE NEEDS TO KNOW (pure, no React): the words that ask for it, the lines it answers as you type, its sample questions ui.tsx HOW IT LOOKS IN THE PANEL (React): its tile in the calculators list, its form, its card and ONE line in src/tools/registry.ts (and one in registry.ui.tsx). My rule: nothing else names a topic. src/lib/tools/detect.ts, src/components/tools/ToolPanel.tsx and the sample-question guide only walk the registry, and src/tools/registry.selftest.ts keeps it that way. This file is the logic side of the contract; the panel side is in uiTypes.ts.

symbols.name: FormCtx
doc: What a form request is checked with: the words of the line, and helpers bound to this topic.

members.name: w
doc: The words of the line, lower case, without punctuation

members.name: has
doc: True when any word of the line is in the set

members.name: only
doc: True when EVERY word is a noun of this topic or a filler ("calculator", "the", "for"), so that "ev policy circular" stays an ordinary search

members.name: calcWord
doc: True when the line has a word like calculator, estimate, compute

symbols.name: HitRule
doc: A typed line that is this topic's own data (a tyre size, a VIN, a sum), which I answer as you type. `kind` names the card; the rest is what the card needs.

members.name: rank
doc: The order in which topics try the line (lower first); see RANKS in detect.ts

members.name: detect
members.type: (q: string, now?: DateTime) => { kind: string } | null

symbols.name: LiveRule
doc: The words of a live-data card ("gold rate today"): I count a line as the card's when it has a key word and every word is a key word, an extra word or a filler.

members.name: phrases
doc: Multi-word names that count as key words and are read as ONE word ("dainik bhaskar"). I need this so that a part of a name that is also a person's name ("bhaskar") never opens the card alone.

members.name: lang
doc: For the news: the tab or language the line asked for (the topic's own words; its card reads it)

symbols.name: IntentInfo
doc: What the topic is, in plain words, for finding it from a line that uses none of its keywords: its name, one sentence about it (read by the AI that is asked what a user means, and shown), and the words and near-words people use for it.

members.name: id
doc: The name of the form (opened with Enter), of the live card, or of the reader

members.name: form
members.type: { rank: number; nouns: string[]; wants: (c: FormCtx) => boolean }
doc: A plain-words request for this topic's form, opened with Enter

members.name: hits
doc: Lines I answer as you type

members.name: intent
doc: What the topic is, for finding it from any line (src/lib/tools/intent.ts)

members.name: samples
doc: Questions for the user guide ("Calculators and converters"); each must really be answered by this topic

symbols.name: defineTopic
symbols.sig: export function defineTopic<const T extends TopicLogic>(t: T): T
doc: I use this to declare a topic and keep its exact types, so that the kinds of its hits and its id reach ToolHit and FormKind without being written anywhere else.
